title: Inter 2-0 Stuttgart: Sucic and Martinez keep automatic qualification hopes alive
subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutInter 2-0 Stuttgart: Sucic and Martinez keep automatic qualification hopes aliveShareInter stretched their winning run in the Champions League to three games with second-half goals from Petar Sucic and Lautaro Martinez.Lautaro Martinez was back on the scoresheet for Inter, who comfortably brushed aside Stuttgart 2-0 in the Champions League.

After struggling to find a way through Stuttgart in the first half, Petar Sucic broke the deadlock from the spot before Martinez scored his first goal since returning from injury to make it three straight Champions League wins for Inter.
Stuttgart made a bright start, with Josep Martinez called into action to deny Chris Fuhrich, but Inter soon grew into the contest at San Siro.
Dennis Seimen was alert to deny Djed Spence on the counter, while Marcus Thuram lashed wide from an angle before Nicolo Barella's low, poked effort hit the inside of the post.

But Inter found their opening in the 57th minute after they were awarded a penalty following a VAR review for a handball against Josha Vagnoman, and Sucic coolly slotted his spot-kick straight down the middle.
Nikolas Nartey was denied by a relieved Yann Bisseck on the line shortly after the hour, but Stuttgart failed to build any momentum before Inter got their second.
Lautaro Martinez was slid through by Federico Dimarco and beat Seimen, with his low strike going in off the inside of the post, securing all three points.
Things were looking dire for Inter after the first two matchdays as they did not have a point to their name, but three straight wins have propelled them up the table into 12th.
They had lost seven of their eight games in the competition prior to this winning streak, but have not even conceded during that run.

Lautaro Martinez scored his 28th goal for Inter in the Champions League, twice as many as any other player for the Nerazzurri in the competition (Adriano - 14). He has recorded a goal involvement in each of his three appearances in the competition this season (three goals, one assist).
And Sucic was also on target, having scored in back-to-back matches for Inter in all competitions for the first time (both penalties).
As for Stuttgart, it was another disappointing European outing as their winless run in the Champions League stretched to three games (D1 L2) after winning their first two.
They have failed to score in consecutive games (having also lost 2-0 to Galatasaray) in the competition for the first time since October 2007.
